recent_events: You catch the monsoon wind and FLY. The ship heels over, sails taut, crew bracing. This is why they call it the Shortcut — if you time it right, nothing's faster.
A small boat with a saffron sail drifts past the Wind Temple headland. Brother Anand sits cross-legged on the deck, eyes closed, reading the wind by feel. His forecast will be posted at dawn.
Wind shifts. The monsoon is changing direction — a day early. Your navigator adjusts instantly. The margin between 'Shortcut' and 'death sentence' is measured in hours.
Whispered conversations below deck. 'How long can we keep sailing?' your bosun hears. He doesn't repeat it.

events.message: An uneventful day at sea.
The Mediterranean in spring is kind. Gentle swells, clear horizons, and a breeze that fills the sails without testing the rigging. The sea remembers how to be generous.
The smell of the sea — salt, kelp, distance. For the crew, this is the smell of possibility. For the captain, it's the smell of responsibility.
Some provisions have spoiled. (-4 days)
An uneventful day at sea.

[bold]You arrive at Corsair's Rest.[/bold]

The port appears through a golden haze — sun-warmed stone, terracotta roofs, and the sound of harbor life carrying across calm water. Spring arrivals in the Mediterranean feel like coming home, even when you've never been here before.

Ships anchor in the hidden cove with no flags flying. A boy in a rowboat approaches to collect the docking fee — payable in silver, no questions.

[bold]One-Eye Basso:[/bold] "...Clear behind you. Come in. Kill your running lights before the bend."

[dim]Landmark: The Cliff Tavern — carved into the rock face, visible only from the sea.[/dim]
[dim]Custom: No names. Every captain here is 'friend' until proven otherwise.[/dim]

The sky is the Mediterranean's trademark blue — the blue that painters have tried to capture for centuries and never quite matched. Your sails look white against it, clean and proud.

The port appears through a golden haze — sun-warmed stone, terracotta roofs, and the sound of harbor life carrying across calm water. Spring arrivals in the Mediterranean feel like coming home, even when you've never been here before.

Sawdust drifts like snow across the waterfront. Half-finished hulls rise on slipways, their ribs exposed like the skeletons of great fish.

[bold]Nuno Ferreira:[/bold] "Berth's over there. Tie up properly — I don't want you drifting into the slipways. Timber loading happens at dawn, so don't sleep late."

[dim]Landmark: The Master Shipyard — where the finest hulls in the Mediterranean take shape.[/dim]
[dim]Custom: Touching another captain's ship without permission is grounds for a duel.[/dim]

[bold]You arrive at Porto Novo.[/bold]

The port appears through a golden haze — sun-warmed stone, terracotta roofs, and the sound of harbor life carrying across calm water. Spring arrivals in the Mediterranean feel like coming home, even when you've never been here before.

Grain barges jostle for position along the stone quays. Clerks with wax tablets tally every bushel while porters sweat under heavy sacks.

[bold]Vasco da Reira:[/bold] "Manifest and tonnage, Captain. I'll assign your berth once I've reviewed them."
[bold]Marta Soares:[/bold] "You're here for the rates? They were posted at dawn. Grain is steady, spice is climbing. What are you buying?"

[dim]Landmark: The Grain Exchange — a columned hall where prices are read aloud at dawn.[/dim]

[bold]You arrive at Monsoon Reach.[/bold]

The port is blooming. Literally — flowers on the docks, garlands on the warehouses, the scent of jasmine mixing with salt air. Spring arrivals in the East Indies feel like being invited to a celebration of survival.

The harbor curves around a headland crowned by the Wind Temple. Ships here are built with deeper keels and stronger masts — the monsoon demands it.

[bold]Harbor Master Ravi:[/bold] "Welcome. The wind is from the southeast today — good for arrivals, not for departures. You'll berth at the headland. The monks will post tomorrow's forecast at dawn."

[dim]Landmark: The Wind Temple — a pagoda on the headland where monks track the monsoon.[/dim]
[dim]Custom: Captains consult the monks before sailing. Their wind forecasts are uncannily accurate.[/dim]
